pairs.evidence: app/_lib/llm-config.ts:334 llmRouteFingerprint looks up only the exact use-case row, but both configuredModelFor (line 294) and the Python resolver (pipeline/jobfit/llm/config.py for_use_case: `use_cases.get(use_case) or use_cases.get("*")`) fall back to the "*" wildcard row, so an operator who re-routes cv_analysis through the wildcard gets an empty fingerprint and the analyze cache serves the previous model's results for the whole TTL.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/llm-config.ts:334 The model-identity input to the cache key is computed by a different lookup than the live route resolution uses, which breaks gate-sees-target: a wildcard-routed model switch leaves the fingerprint at "" and the stamp never changes.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/_components/voice/transport/openai.ts:173 speakText concatenates the intake agent's LLM reply (prior model output, which the standard classes as untrusted) straight onto the per-response instruction after a bare newline, with no declared insertion point or fence, so payload text is read by the realtime model as part of its own instructions; the <<END>> sentinel that was once read aloud (app/api/intake/reply-sentinel.ts) is this bleed showing up.

techniques.evidence: app/_components/voice/transport/openai.ts:173 An untrusted span (model reply passed in from JdsIntakeVoice data.reply) is interpolated into the instruction field with no trust class, delimiter or fence.
app/_components/voice/transport/elevenlabs.ts:172 The interviewer prompt is assembled on the server and the client only forwards it verbatim; it adds no prompt text of its own on this path.
app/_components/voice/transport/openai.ts:292 In the agent-held realtime protocol the client sends only deltas (one directive item) and never edits or compacts the provider-held conversation.

app/_components/voice/transport/elevenlabs.ts:196 Client tools are registered from the single director vocabulary rather than a hand-written list, so the registered tools cannot drift from the dispatcher.
